short_answer: Sports Information Traders is a real business with a Beverly Hills address, a toll free number, written terms and a named lead handicapper, Jon Price. Price has a Wikipedia page and has appeared on sports radio, and articles about him go back to 2015. In that narrow sense the service is legitimate.

Whether the picks make money is a separate question that nothing we opened answers. The site publishes no record and no prices, and its picks pages ask for a password. Every win rate we found, from "6 Wins, 2 Losses, and 1 Push" to 130 of 160, traces back to Price or to articles that are promotional or labeled sponsored.

The little independent discussion we found is skeptical. In a 2016 Covers forum thread an account writing as Jon Price promoted the service, was asked for a documented record, did not give one, and is now shown as banned. Treat SIT as a phone sold service with marketing claims and no checkable record, and note that the terms rule out refunds and guarantees.
pricing_intro: We found no prices on sportsinformationtraders.com on 16 Nov 2026. The packages page lists two offers by name only and sends buyers to the phone line.
pricing: No terms stated on the packages page
No terms stated; a 2015 Card Player article described it as syndicate plays with live text alerts
guarantee: The current terms say "ALL SALES ARE FINAL, AND NO REFUNDS ARE PROVIDED," that consulting fees are fully earned upon payment, and "There are no warranties or guarantees regarding our services." They also say the service is intended solely for entertainment and that SIT's selections are not guaranteed.

That is very different from older marketing. A 2015 Card Player article said the company would "guarantee you'll make money on your investment" and described a 90 day trial program, with no written terms. Go by the current terms: once you pay, you should not expect any money back, and betting losses are never covered.

claims_note: The start date is not consistent. Wikipedia says Price began selling picks in 2013, while the site says he has handicapped for 20+ years. Both can be true, but buyers should know the pick selling business itself dates from about 2013 by that account.
Gambling911 cites a 63% career figure from a body it calls the LV Sportsbook Commission. We could not identify any such body, and Price said the real number is higher without giving one.
The site's own counters for "Clients Advised" and "Straight Winning Seasons" were blank on 16 Nov 2026.
record: What a buyer can verify independently: nothing that we could find. We found no full, time stamped log of every SIT pick with the line, the odds and the release time, and no third party tracking of the service.
What the seller publishes: on 16 Nov 2026 the Picks and Access Picks pages both asked for a password. The free content is daily betting previews and articles. No results table was visible.

Every win rate we found came from Price himself or from articles about him that are promotional, guest submitted or labeled sponsored. A 2015 interview has Price saying the goal is "winning between 60-65 percent of the plays," which is far above what verified long run bettors achieve.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition no Sports Information Traders pick history is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how Sports Information Traders performs.
our_data.context: For scale: SIT marketing talks about 60 to 65% winners and spring runs above 80%. On the Watchdog board on 16 Nov 2026, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard odds of 110 to win 100 a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Independent customer evidence on Sports Information Traders is thin. Most pages about the service are interviews and features built around Jon Price. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: We found almost no first hand buyer reports. The positive material, in Card Player (2015), Gambling911 (2015), BroBible (2017, labeled sponsored) and Awful Announcing (2021), all repeats figures from Price or his staff. The only forum discussion we could open was one Covers promotion thread from 2016: an account writing as Price promoted the service, other members asked for a documented record and did not get one, and one member said a friend who bought the picks had not come close to 50%. That is a single secondhand report, so it shows skepticism, not a pattern. We found no positive buyer report outside the seller's own media.

In a Covers forum promotion thread, a member wrote that a friend bought some of Price's picks and "hasn't been close to 50%". This is a secondhand account with no record attached, and we could not verify it.

The same Covers thread was opened by an account writing in the first person as Jon Price, claiming he called the Denver Broncos Super Bowl run and that SIT clients had a lucrative NFL season. Most of the 24 replies were skeptical: they said many people picked Denver, one season proves little, and he showed no documented record. The account now shows as banned on Covers.

A Card Player feature built on an interview with Price called SIT "the premier sports investment service in the world" and repeated his claims of an 8 and 0 run for a poker player and a $200K winnings check. No record was shown, and the page carries no paid content label, but the claims are all Price's.
A BroBible article labeled sponsored followed SIT picks for two weekends and reported 6 wins, 2 losses and 1 push. Nine picks say nothing about long run results.
Awful Announcing reported that Price went 130 for 160 in the spring of 2021. The article gives no source or log for the figure, and the commentary around it comes from Price.

A Better Business Bureau search for Sports Information Traders in Beverly Hills returned no results. Two Sportsbook Review threads that mention Price no longer opened, and our web searches found no TheRX thread and no court or regulator action naming SIT or Price.

conflicts: The Picks and Access Picks pages carry a "Get $1,500 in Bonus Bets" banner that links through a BetMGM partner tracking address. Affiliate deals usually pay the referrer when referred customers sign up or bet. That does not prove anything about the picks, but it is a financial interest a buyer should know about.
Much of the coverage of Price is labeled sponsored, guest submitted, or built on his own interview answers. Read those articles as marketing.
strengths: A named business with a Beverly Hills address, a toll free number and written terms.
A named lead handicapper with years of radio and press appearances, so you know who is behind the picks.
The terms are blunt about risk: no guarantees, entertainment only, and a problem gambling helpline.
concerns: No prices on the site. You have to call, which puts the pricing in a sales conversation.
All sales are final and no refunds are provided, while older marketing promised that clients would make money.
No full public record. Picks pages are password protected and every win rate comes from Price or promotional articles.
The only forum discussion we could open was skeptical, and the account promoting SIT there is shown as banned.
Win rate claims of 60 to 65% and higher are far above what verified long run bettors achieve.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Get the price and the terms in writing before you pay. These terms say all sales are final.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: It is a real business with an address, a phone number, written terms and a named lead handicapper, Jon Price. We could not verify that its picks win over time, because it publishes no record, and we found no court or regulator action involving it.
How much does Sports Information Traders cost?
We could not find out. On 16 Nov 2026 the site listed a 50% NFL Season Special with no price and a Private Investor Group marked "Call For Details". Pricing is given over the phone.
Does Sports Information Traders offer refunds?
No. The terms say all sales are final, no refunds are provided, fees are fully earned upon payment, and there are no warranties or guarantees.
Is Sports Information Traders worth it?

What you get is picks from a named handicapper with a media profile. What is unproven is whether those picks beat the roughly 52.4% needed at standard odds over hundreds of plays. With no public prices, no record and no refunds, a buyer carries all the risk.
